prompt:
You are illustrating a plate for PRIME DISpatch, an editorial scrollytelling magazine
documenting the construction of Prime City. Produce ONE finished editorial illustration.

THE BRIEF
The DISpatch building — the first published Building in Prime City's Editorial District.

A modest civic press house, three or four storeys, drawn complete and in full detail: printing floor,
loading bay, a reading room, stacked paper, a small courtyard. It stands finished and inhabited.

Around it, the rest of the district is still being drafted. Neighbouring blocks fade outward from
fully rendered, to line-only elevations, to bare lot lines and surveyor's marks on empty paper — a
city caught mid-construction, one building at a time. Scaffolding and a crane at the far edge.
Street grid and block boundaries run underneath everything as fine ruled lines.

Axonometric, viewed from above and slightly to one side, the way a drafting office would present a
completed parcel to a city record. The finished building is the visual anchor; the unbuilt district
around it is quiet and sparse.

THE HOUSE REGISTER (read off the shipped banner corpus — match it)
Editorial illustration in the register of a hand-drawn architectural plate — the kind of
drawing a small press would print on good paper.

  - Medium: ink line work. Pen, technical drafting pen, or fine brush. Visible hatching and
    stipple for tone. The paper grain and the warmth of the stock are part of the image.
  - View: axonometric, isometric, or straight top-down plan. A drafted view, never a
    photographic one — the drawing knows it is a drawing.
  - Subject: architecture and the city. Buildings in section or cut-away, rooftops, street
    grids, lot lines, scaffolding and cranes, surveyor's marks, the machinery of construction.
  - Density: rich and patient. Small incidental detail rewards a second look — the drawing
    should hold up when the reader stops scrolling and looks properly.
  - Colour: the paper ground plus one or two accent pigments, used sparingly as marks,
    annotations, and network lines. Never a wash, never a gradient, never a field of colour.
  - Figures: if present, small, silhouetted, incidental to the architecture. No portraits.
  - Temperature: warm, quiet, restrained, precise. Civic-archive, not science fiction.

THE PALETTE — use these values and essentially nothing else (dawn cycle)
  - #f6f1e7  — the paper ground — everything sits on this
  - #ded3bb  — the deepest paper tone, for shadow and weight
  - #14110c  — the ink — line work and hatching
  - #8e2532  — wine — dispatch-precious, a rare small accent, NEVER a wash or gradient
  - #bb4812  — terracotta — the editorial lane accent
  - #3b4b62  — graphite-blue — the institutional lane accent
  - #b87333  — copper — wayfinding marks and fine annotation
  Ground: warm pale vellum paper — the default published surface.
  The palette is deliberately narrow and low-chroma. Chrome is never vivid. Wine is
  precious: at most a few small marks, never a field, never a gradient, never a wash.

COMPOSITION
  - Aspect ratio 4:3. The plate is cropped with object-fit: cover inside a tall
    column on desktop and a wide strip on mobile, so keep the subject centred and leave the
    outer eighth of every edge free of anything load-bearing.
  - Flat or axonometric. Architectural, drafted, top-down or elevated — never a street-level
    eye-line, never a first-person view.

HARD CONSTRAINTS — a plate violating any of these is discarded
  - NO lettering of any kind. No words, no captions, no signage, no numerals, no logos, no
    wordmark. The publication sets its own type over this plate in Vollkorn, Crimson Pro, Pangram Sans, JetBrains Mono — a
    drawn word would collide with it, and a drawn "DISpatch" would break the wordmark split
    rule that governs every rendering of that word without exception. Leave the type quiet
    room; do not draw the type.
  - NO photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy or cinematic lighting, no lens flare, no bokeh.
    This is ink and printed paper.
  - NO neon, no cyberpunk teal-and-magenta, no glow, no chrome gradients.
  - NO UI mockups, no dashboards, no browser windows, no device frames.
  - NO human faces in focus. Figures, if any, are small, silhouetted, and incidental.
  - Canon tombstone: Street-view cartography, literal cosmology labeling ("this is the Governance Pillar"), or substrate animation at scroll cadence

The result should read as a hand-drawn plate from a small editorial press — an architectural
document that happens to be beautiful. Restrained, warm, quiet, and precise.
